extraction_text: Janamejaya asks about the nature of devotion to the single God, who is most beloved by Hari, and its origins.
Sauti recounts the context of the Mahabharata war, where Arjuna was despondent and Krishna personally instructed him.
Sauti states that Yudhishthira once asked the sage Narada this same question about devotion in the presence of Krishna and Bhishma.

attributes.relationship: Yudhishthira seeks wisdom from sage Narada

extraction_text: Sauti explains that his teacher Vyasa narrated Narada's response about the origin and transmission of this devotion.
Narada describes how Brahma originated from Narayana's heart/mouth and that Narayana himself first practiced this devotion, offering sacrifices to gods and ancestors.
The devotion was obtained by water-drinking sages, then passed to Vekhanasas, then to Soma, before disappearing.
Brahma is born again from Narayana's eyes, learns the devotion from Soma, and teaches it to Rudra, who has Narayana as his soul.
In the Krita Yuga, Rudra, practicing yoga, chants this devotion to all dwarf sages before it disappears again due to the Great God's illusion.
Brahma is born a third time from Narayana's speech, and the devotion arises directly from Narayana again.
The sage Garuda, through severe austerities, self-control, and observance, obtains this devotion from the Supreme Person.
Garuda chants this supreme devotion three times daily, leading to the vow being known in the world as the 'Three Garuda Vow'.
The Rigveda chants this difficult vow; Vayu, the lifespan of the world, learns this eternal devotion from Garuda.
Leftover-eating sages obtain the devotion from Vayu, then the ocean obtains it from them, before it disappears again, merging into Narayana.
Brahma is born once more from Narayana's ear, as Narada continues his narration.
Hari Narayana conceived the idea of creating the world and desired a creator.
Brahma emerged from Hari Narayana's ear to become the creator of all beings.
Hari Narayana instructed Brahma to create all beings from his mouth and feet, granting him power and radiance.
Hari Narayana bestowed the Shatvata Dharma and Aranyaka texts upon Brahma.
Brahma accepted the teachings and bowed to Hari Narayana.
Hari Narayana identified the Shatvata Dharma as the law for the Satya Yuga and departed to the realm of the unmanifest.
Brahma created all movable and immovable beings in the world.
The Satya Yuga began with Shatvata Dharma pervading all worlds.
Brahma worshipped Hari Narayana according to the primordial dharma.
Brahma transmitted the dharma to Svarajisha Manu for establishing it in the world.
Svarajisha Manu transmitted the dharma to his son Shankhapada.
Shankhapada transmitted the dharma to his son, the guardian of directions.
The dharma disappeared at the beginning of the Treta Yuga.
Brahma was reborn from Hari Narayana's nose, and Hari Narayana personally recited the dharma before him.
Brahma's son Nityayuvan learned the dharma.
At the beginning of Satya Yuga, Prajapati Varuna learned the dharma from Nityayuvan.
Varuna taught the dharma to Laugya, who taught it to his son Kuchi.

attributes.relationship: Teacher to disciple, father to son

extraction_text: The dharma disappeared again.
After Brahma was born from an egg, the dharma was recited to him by Narada.
Brahma accepted and practiced the dharma, then taught it to the Bhrishada sages.
The sages taught it to Jayashtha, who taught it to King Avikampana.
The dharma disappeared again.
After Brahma's seventh birth from a lotus, Hari Narayana personally recited the dharma and taught it to Brahma.
Brahma transmitted the dharma to Daksha.
Daksha taught it to Aditya, who taught it to Vivasvat.
At the beginning of Treta Yuga, Vivasvat taught the dharma to Manu, who taught it to his son King Ikshvaku.

attributes.relationship: Teacher to disciple, father to son

extraction_text: The text describes the transmission of a sacred law (Dharma) from its origin through various divine and sage figures.
The law is described as eternal, difficult to understand, and upheld by the Shatvata clan.
Hari (Narayana) is described in various forms and as the supreme being, soul, creator, and sustainer.
The law of devotion to the one god (Narayana) is explained, leading to liberation.
King Janamejaya questions why different Brahmins follow different laws instead of the same one.
Shaunaka explains the three gunas (qualities) related to the body, with sattva (goodness) being superior and leading to liberation through Narayana.
It is stated that only with Narayana's attention does a person awaken; one cannot awaken by their own will alone.

divine_elements: Necessity of divine grace for spiritual awakening

extraction_text: 护民子 explains the nature of gunas (qualities) and how they affect individuals' spiritual paths, mentioning that Hari (Vishnu) does not focus on those with mixed rajas and tamas, while Brahma attends to them.

attributes.relationships: 护民子 is instructing 镇群
attributes.divine_elements: Mentions Hari (Vishnu), Brahma, and the concept of gunas

extraction_text: 镇群 asks how those who are changeable (due to lack of sattva) can reach the Supreme Person.

attributes.relationships: 镇群 seeks clarification from 护民子

extraction_text: 护民子 responds that one can reach the Supreme Person (the 25th tattva) by renouncing action, and describes various scriptures (Sankhya, Yoga, Vedas, etc.) as consistent and focused on worshipping Narayana.

attributes.relationships: 护民子 continues teaching 镇群
attributes.divine_elements: Mentions Narayana, the 25th tattva, and various scriptures

extraction_text: 护民子 states that this teaching (Shatvata Dharma) was told to him by his teacher Vyasa, who heard it from Narada, and that it is difficult to practice.

attributes.relationships: 护民子 learned from Vyasa, who learned from Narada
attributes.divine_elements: Mentions Narada as a divine sage

extraction_text: 护民子 mentions that Krishna (Hari) both creates and bewilders the world.

attributes.divine_elements: Attributes creative and bewildering powers to Krishna

extraction_text: In the next chapter, 镇群 asks about the relationship between various scriptures (Sankhya, Yoga, Pancharatra, Vedas, Aranyakas).

attributes.relationships: 镇群 seeks further clarification from 护民子

extraction_text: 护民子 praises Vyasa (also known as Island-born or Krishna Dvaipayana) as an incarnation of Narayana, a great sage who dispels ignorance and is a treasury of the Vedas.

attributes.relationships: 护民子 reveres Vyasa as his teacher and a divine incarnation
attributes.divine_elements: Describes Vyasa as an incarnation of Narayana and son of Brahma

extraction_text: 镇群 points out a contradiction: earlier it was said Vyasa was the son of Parashara (破灭), but now he is called the son of Narayana.

attributes.relationships: 镇群 notes familial lineage (Vyasa as son of Parashara) versus divine lineage (son of Narayana)

extraction_text: 镇群 asks 护民子 to explain how Vyasa was born from Narayana and what his previous birth was.

attributes.action: Request for clarification on Vyasa's divine birth
attributes.relationships: 镇群 seeks deeper explanation from 护民子

extraction_text: Vyasa (the teacher) completed the creation of the Mahabharata story at the foot of the Snowy Mountain (Himalayas).
Vyasa was surrounded and served by his five noble students: Sumantu, Jaimini, Vaisampayana, Suka (Vyasa's son), and the narrator (Paila).

attributes.relationships: Teacher-Student, Father-Son

extraction_text: The students asked Vyasa to explain the meaning of the Vedas, the meaning of the Mahabharata story, and how he was born from Narayana.
Vyasa began narrating a primordial sacred story he learned through asceticism.
Brahma was born for the seventh time from a lotus when the great yogi Narayana, free from good and evil, created the infinitely radiant Brahma from his navel.
Narayana commanded Brahma to create all kinds of beings, wise or foolish.
Brahma, filled with anxiety and feeling incapable, bowed to the beneficent great god Hari (Narayana) and asked for arrangements to be made.
After hearing Brahma, the lord god (Narayana) disappeared and summoned the goddess Wisdom within his heart.
Wisdom appeared beside Hari. The transcendent great god used yoga to retain her.
The eternal, unchanging god (Narayana) commanded the capable goddess Wisdom, established in supreme yoga, to enter Brahma for the purpose of world creation.
Wisdom quickly entered Brahma. Seeing Brahma united with Wisdom, Hari again commanded him to create all kinds of beings.
After speaking, the lord god (Narayana) disappeared and instantly returned to his own heavenly abode.

The lord god (Narayana) restored to his original, unified form, then conceived another thought: to alleviate the earth's burden caused by powerful Daityas, Danavas, Gandharvas, and Rakshasas who might become arrogant after gaining boons through asceticism.

Narayana resolved to take various avatars on earth as situations required, to punish evil and support good, and to support the honest, struggling earth by becoming the serpent beneath it to hold it up.
Narayana (Vishnu) decides to take avatars to protect the earth.
Narayana creates various forms for his avatars: Boar, Man-Lion, Dwarf, and Man.

attributes.purpose: To destroy enemies of the gods

extraction_text: Narayana produces the goddess of speech Sarasvati and then produces Sarasvata (also known as Apantaratama).

attributes.relationships: Sarasvata is created as a son of Narayana

extraction_text: Narayana instructs Sarasvata to compile the Vedas.
Sarasvata compiles the Vedas during the Svayambhuva Manu period.
Narayana (Hari) is pleased with Sarasvata's work, austerities, self-control, and observances.
Narayana prophesies that Sarasvata will be the world's mover in every Manu period and will compile Vedas again in the Kali Yuga.
Narayana prophesies that the Bharata/Kuru kings will split, disobey Sarasvata, and destroy each other.
Narayana mentions that Vasistha, born from Brahma's mind, will be Sarasvata's father in a future birth through an unmarried maiden.

attributes.relationships: Vasistha will be father to Sarasvata's reincarnation

extraction_text: Narayana grants Sarasvata insight into past and future ages and a vision of himself as eternal with the discus.
Narayana states that Shani (Saturn) will be a great Manu and Sarasvata will be superior to the seven sages.
Narayana dismisses Sarasvata after speaking.
Vyasa narrates that he was born as Apantaratama (Sarasvata) by Hari's grace, then reborn as a descendant of Vasistha.

attributes.relationships: Vyasa is the reincarnation of Sarasvata/Apantaratama, descendant of Vasistha

extraction_text: Vyasa explains his origin as a portion of Narayana and recounts his past austerities and meditation.
Vyasa concludes by stating he has shared his past and future due to the listeners' reverence and questions.
护民子讲述毗耶娑的前生，并介绍各种知识和学说：数论、瑜伽、五夜经、吠陀、兽主经。

attributes.relationships: 护民子为讲述者，毗耶娑为被提及的老师

extraction_text: 迦比罗大仙宣讲数论，古老的金胎通晓瑜伽。

attributes.relationships: 迦比罗与数论关联，金胎与瑜伽关联

extraction_text: 阿般多罗多摩是吠陀导师，有些人称他为古胎。

attributes.relationships: 阿般多罗多摩是吠陀导师，别名古胎

extraction_text: 梵天的儿子吉项（又名湿婆，乌玛之夫）宣讲兽主经。

attributes.relationships: 吉项是梵天的儿子，又名湿婆，乌玛的丈夫

extraction_text: 那罗延通晓全部五夜经，是至高归宿和经典创造者。

attributes.action: 通晓知识，被视为至高存在
attributes.relationships: 那罗延是知识掌握者和创造者

extraction_text: 镇群询问原人的数量、至高原人及万物之源。

attributes.relationships: 镇群为提问者

extraction_text: 护民子解释数论者和瑜伽行者认为有许多原人，但许多原人有一个起源，即充满性质的宇宙。

attributes.relationships: 护民子为解释者，引用毗耶娑的观点

extraction_text: 护民子向毗耶娑致敬，描述毗耶娑为具有苦行、控制自我的大仙。

attributes.relationships: 护民子尊敬毗耶娑为老师

attributes.relationships: 湿婆是梵天从额头生出的儿子

extraction_text: 梵天经常从威罗阇宫来到威阇衍多山，独自思索内在灵魂。

attributes.relationships: 梵天为思索者

extraction_text: 湿婆（瑜伽之主）偶然从空中来到威阇衍多山。

attributes.relationships: 湿婆为瑜伽之主

extraction_text: Rudra descended from the sky, landed on the mountaintop, and appeared before Brahma, joyfully touching his feet in reverence.
Brahma, the Supreme Creator, lifted Rudra up with his left hand.
Brahma welcomed his long-absent son, inquired about his well-being, and asked about his studies of the Vedas and practice of austerities.

Rudra responded that everything was well due to Brahma's grace, mentioned their previous meeting in the Viraja palace, and expressed curiosity about why Brahma was alone in this secluded mountain spot.

Rudra questioned why Brahma left his unparalleled palace—which was free from hunger and thirst, inhabited by radiant gods, asuras, and sages, and accompanied by gandharvas and apsaras—to come alone to this high mountain.

attributes.relationship: Son seeking wisdom from creator father

extraction_text: Brahma explained that he frequently comes to this lofty Vajayanta mountain to meditate and contemplate the luminous Purusha (the Cosmic Being).
Rudra expressed confusion, noting that Brahma as Ishvara (the Supreme Lord) created many purushas and everything else, and asked which supreme purusha Brahma was contemplating.

attributes.relationship: Disciple-like inquiry from son to father

extraction_text: Brahma described this Purusha as transcending all other purushas, being the foundation yet invisible, the sole source of all purushas, identical with the supreme cosmic universe, eternal and free from qualities, into whom all quality-free beings merge.

attributes.supernatural_element: Description of the transcendent Cosmic Being/Purusha
